steps.title: Edit here, the build picks it up
steps.body:
Never edit `build/src/` directly, because it is disposable and gets recreated. Put your changes in the places in the left column; the middle column shows which script consumes them and the right column where they end up.

The tour follows the rows from top to bottom.

steps.title: local.conf configures every script
steps.body:
Versions, passwords, packages, hostname and `BUILD_DIR` live here. Every script reads it, so it affects everything.

It is the first file to edit for anything that is a setting rather than code.

steps.title: Boot firmware patches go into imx-boot.bin
steps.body:
U-Boot patches are applied by `uboot.sh` step 3 and TF-A patches by step 2. Both end up in `imx-boot.bin` at 32 KiB, with the TF-A one in the BL31 part.

Create them with `git format-patch`.

steps.title: Kernel code and options end up in /boot
steps.body:
Source patches and config fragments (`CONFIG_FOO=y`) are applied by `kernel.sh`. Either way the result is `/boot/Image.gz` and the modules.

A fragment is the smaller change, so use one when an option is enough.

steps.title: Your carrier's device tree becomes a .dtb in /boot
steps.body:
`kernel.sh dtbs` compiles your device tree and writes `/boot/<name>.dtb`.

U-Boot then needs `fdt_file` to name it.

steps.title: Users, network and services shape the Debian root
steps.body:
`rootfs.sh` runs this script, and the result is `/` on partition 1.

Changes here do not touch the kernel or the bootloader.

steps.title: uEnv.txt needs no rebuild
steps.body:
It lives on the card and overrides boot-time variables such as `fdt_file` and `kernelargs`. U-Boot reads it at every boot.

It is the quickest way to test a change.

steps.anchor: Then rebuild only what changed: ./build.sh uboot | kernel | rootfs, then ./build.sh image, or update a card in place with flash --kernel-only / --bootloader-only.
steps.title: Takeaway: rebuild only what changed
steps.body: Run `./build.sh uboot`, `kernel` or `rootfs` as needed, then `./build.sh image`. Or update a card in place with `flash --kernel-only` or `--bootloader-only`.
